# Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. (HLT) — Q2 2026 Earnings Digest

**Classification:** editor-authored digest of public IR — decision support  
**Prepared:** 2026-09-20 ET  
**Period:** Quarter ended 2026-06-30  
**Call / release date:** 2026-07-28 (release + call ~09:00 ET)

## Sources

- **company release / 8-K exhibit:** Hilton Reports Second Quarter Results — SEC HTML exhibit  
  https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1585689/000158568926000042/q22026earningsrelease.htm  
  (`company release` / `8-K`)
- **company IR mirror:** https://ir.hilton.com/news-events/investor-news/detail/85/hilton-reports-second-quarter-results (`company release`)
- **slides / highlight PDF:** https://stories-editor.hilton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/HLT.Q2-2026-Results-JUL2026-L08FINAL.pdf — mirrored `_raw/HLT_Q2_2026_Results.pdf` (`slides`)
- **10-Q:** filed ~2026-07-28 — https://ir.hilton.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001585689-26-000043/hlt-20260630.htm (`10-Q`)
- **Stories From Hilton syndication:** https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-reports-2026-second-quarter-results (`company release`)

*Transcript:* not opened this pass (webcast replay may be free on IR; Seeking Alpha often paywalled) — treat call color as **not used** unless cited below from the written release.

---

## Capital headline

Hilton’s Q2 print is a **fee-platform compounding** quarter, not an owned-RevPAR story: system-wide comparable RevPAR +3.9% currency-neutral with management + franchise fees +6.4%, Adjusted EBITDA $1.054B, and **record development pipeline** (541,300 rooms) with net unit growth running 6.1% trailing. Management is returning capital at scale (~$3.5B FY capital-return guide; $966M returned in Q2 incl. dividends) while terming out debt ($1.0B 5.500% notes due 2031). For Capital Graph: owners still fund bricks; Hilton monetizes brand density, conversions, and new lifestyle/midscale product (Undergraduate by Hilton). MEA RevPAR −29.5% is the clear geographic risk flag — do not extrapolate U.S. strength globally.

## Operating KPIs (company-reported only)

| Metric | Q2 2026 | vs Q2 2025 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| System-wide comparable RevPAR (currency neutral) | — | **+3.9%** | company release |
| System-wide OCC | **74.9%** | +1.0 pts | company release (stats table) |
| System-wide ADR | **$166.97** | +2.5% | company release |
| System-wide RevPAR ($) | **$125.02** | +3.9% | company release |
| U.S. RevPAR | $139.28 | **+5.4%** | company release |
| Americas ex-U.S. RevPAR | $108.32 | +4.6% | company release |
| Europe RevPAR | $143.28 | +4.3% | company release |
| Middle East & Africa RevPAR | $93.65 | **−29.5%** | company release |
| Asia Pacific RevPAR | $66.80 | +1.2% | company release |
| Mgmt + franchise fee revenues | — | **+6.4%** | company release |
| Franchise & licensing fees ($) | **$808M** | vs $745M | company release / 10-Q |
| Base & other management fees | **$99M** | vs $97M | company release |
| Incentive management fees | **$69M** | vs $75M | company release |
| Diluted EPS | **$2.10** | vs $1.84 | company release |
| Diluted EPS, adj. special items | **$2.29** | vs $2.20 | company release |
| Net income | **$482M** | vs $442M | company release |
| Adjusted EBITDA | **$1,054M** | vs $1,008M | company release |
| Adj. EBITDA margin (company-defined) | **76.6%** | vs 75.2% | company release |
| STR / competitive-set RevPAR index | **not disclosed** | — | — |

YTD (6M): system-wide comparable RevPAR +3.9%; mgmt+franchise fees +8.3%; Adj. EBITDA $1,955M (`company release`).

## Outlook & guidance

**Full year 2026** (`company release`):

- System-wide comparable RevPAR (currency neutral): **+3.0% to +3.5%** vs 2025  
  - Q3 expected to benefit from World Cup + favorable calendar; Q4 pressured by unfavorable calendar + midterm elections  
- Diluted EPS: $8.22–$8.35; adj. diluted EPS: **$8.89–$9.01**  
- Net income: $1,883–$1,911M  
- Adjusted EBITDA: **$4,040–$4,080M**  
- Net unit growth: **6.0%–7.0%** (2H expected to outperform 1H)  
- Capital return: **~$3.5B**  
- Contract acquisition costs + CapEx (ex third-party reimbursed): **~$300M**  
- G&A: **~$400M**

**Q3 2026:** system-wide comparable RevPAR **~+4.0%**; Adj. EBITDA $1,035–$1,055M; adj. diluted EPS $2.28–$2.34 (`company release`).

CFO note: Q2 NI / Adj. EBITDA benefited from better-than-expected RevPAR and **$17M of non-RevPAR items** pulled forward from 2H (`company release`).

## Supply, pipeline, conversions, renovations / CapEx

- Opened **207 hotels / 24,100 rooms**; **21,600 net** rooms in Q2; openings **+50%** seq. vs Q1 (`company release`)  
- Approvals **42,900** rooms in Q2 (second-largest approvals quarter in company history per highlight PDF) (`slides` / `company release`)  
- Pipeline **3,853 hotels / 541,300 rooms** across 132 countries/territories as of 2026-06-30; **+6%** rooms vs YE prior-year compare; almost half under construction; **>50%** rooms outside U.S. (`company release`)  
- Trailing net unit growth **6.1%** (Jun 2025 → Jun 2026) for managed/franchised/strategic partner hotels (`slides` / `company release`)  
- New brand: **Undergraduate by Hilton** (upper-midscale / college-university markets); long-term growth potential cited as **>400 hotels** (`slides`)  
- Notable: Conrad Athens The Ilisian; first three **Apartment Collection by Hilton**; Waldorf Astoria Miami Beach signing (`company release`)  
- Q2 CapEx + contract acquisition costs: **$88M** (CapEx $37M + contract acquisition $51M net) (`company release`)  
- System size: **9,332 hotels / 1,363,441 rooms** (+ HGV timeshare system total 9,453 / 1,384,842) (`company release`)

**supply note:** pipeline conversion rate + Undergraduate / Apartment Collection absorption; conversion vs new-build mix.

## Balance sheet / debt / refinancing

- Debt outstanding **$13.4B** (ex deferred financing/discount); WA rate **5.03%**; ex finance leases $13.1B @ 5.04% (`company release`)  
- No material maturities until **Apr 2029** other than **$600M** Senior Notes due **Apr 2027** (`company release`)  
- May 2026: issued **$1.0B** 5.500% Senior Notes due **2031**; repaid $450M revolver draws (`company release`)  
- Revolver: **$0** drawn; available capacity **$1,894M** after $106M LCs (`company release`)  
- Cash & equivalents **$1,064M** incl. $55M restricted (`company release`)  
- Net debt **$12,380M**; net debt / TTM Adj. EBITDA **3.2x** (`company release`)  
- Buybacks: Q2 **2.9M** shares @ avg **$326.99** = **$932M**; YTD **5.6M** shares / **$1,826M** incl. dividends path; capital return YTD through July **$2,034M** (`company release`)  
- Dividend $0.15/share; Sep 30, 2026 payment authorized (`company release`)  
- Shares out ~**225.1M** as of 2026-07-23 (`company release`)

**capital note:** 2027 $600M notes refinance path; leverage stable IG fee model; buyback pace vs net unit growth reinvestment (key money / contract acquisition).

## Labor / talent / cost

- Named No. 1 best workplace in nine countries (Great Place To Work) — brand/talent PR (`slides`)  
- Wage/staffing dollar metrics: **not disclosed** in release tables beyond G&A guide (~$400M FY)  
- Risk factors cite labor shortages/disputes (`company release` forward-looking section)

**talent note:** soft talent brand signal only; no wage inflation quantification in this release.

## Segment / brand / geography mix

- **Fee engine dominates:** franchise/licensing $808M vs ownership revenue $311M in Q2 (`company release`)  
- Ownership segment RevPAR **−3.4%** (ADR −4.8%) vs management/franchise RevPAR **+4.0%** — owned book is not the growth story (`company release`)  
- Brand standouts (RevPAR y/y): Graduate +8.8%, Tapestry +6.6%, Home2 +5.9%, LXR +5.8%, Tru +5.1%, Embassy +5.2%; Waldorf Astoria −1.1%, Conrad flat (`company release`)  
- U.S. (+5.4% RevPAR) carries the system; MEA (−29.5%) is the stress geography (`company release`)

## Capital Graph signal proposals (decision support)

1. **Signal:** Hilton system RevPAR growth mid-single-digit with fee growth outpacing RevPAR (fees +6.4% vs RevPAR +3.9%).  
   **Domain:** D1 (KPIs) / F* (brand fees)  
   **Evidence:** company release Q2 2026  
   **Implication:** Fee platforms still extract growth via mix/net units even when unit RevPAR is mid-single digit — underwrite franchisee cash-flow capacity, not just brand RevPAR.  
   **Lane:** demand | none for STR invent

2. **Signal:** Pipeline at record 541,300 rooms; NUG guide 6–7%; approvals +50% seq.  
   **Domain:** C2 / C5 (supply / brand network)  
   **Evidence:** company release + slides  
   **Implication:** Near-term fee CAGR visibility high; watch conversion share vs ground-up as construction costs bite owners.  
   **Lane:** supply

3. **Signal:** Undergraduate by Hilton + Apartment Collection — midscale/lifestyle/extended product expansion.  
   **Domain:** C5 / F*  
   **Evidence:** company release / slides  
   **Implication:** Hilton competing harder for owner capital in upper-midscale & residential-adjacent — franchisee CapEx and PIP standards matter for AAHOA-type owners.  
   **Lane:** supply | talent

4. **Signal:** MEA RevPAR −29.5% — geopolitical / regional demand shock inside an otherwise healthy system.  
   **Domain:** A* (demand color)  
   **Evidence:** company release regional table  
   **Implication:** Do not use global system RevPAR as a uniform capital signal; region-weight underwriting.  
   **Lane:** demand

5. **Signal:** ~$3.5B FY capital return + net debt/EBITDA 3.2x + 2031 notes issue.  
   **Domain:** E2 (debt / capital structure)  
   **Evidence:** company release  
   **Implication:** IG feeco continues to run leverage for buybacks; 2027 maturity is manageable but schedule it.  
   **Lane:** capital

6. **Signal:** Q3 RevPAR guide ~+4% aided by World Cup / calendar; Q4 guide soft factors (elections/calendar).  
   **Domain:** D1 / A*  
   **Evidence:** company release Outlook  
   **Implication:** 2H is not linear — event/calendar residual risk for owner REITs sharing the calendar.  
   **Lane:** demand | Host/Park digests

## What Hal should decide / watch

- Whether **6–7% NUG** remains credible if owner financing stays tight (conversions vs new-build).  
- **MEA** duration and any franchisee distress flags in that region.  
- Buyback vs **key money / contract acquisition** ($51M Q2) — who captures surplus.  
- Q3 World Cup / calendar beat vs Q4 election drag — sequence CapEx/deploy.  
- Competitive response: Marriott/Hyatt soft-brand and midscale pushes vs Undergraduate.

## Quotes worth keeping

> “Our disciplined development strategy continues to drive strong results, with openings and approvals both increasing 50 percent sequentially from the first quarter and our pipeline ending the quarter at a record level.” — Christopher J. Nassetta, President & CEO (`company release`)

> “We remain confident in our ability to deliver net unit growth of 6.0% to 7.0% in 2026 and beyond.” — Nassetta (`company release`)

# Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. (HST) — Q2 2026 Earnings Digest

**Classification:** editor-authored digest of public IR — decision support  
**Prepared:** 2026-09-20 ET  
**Period:** Quarter ended 2026-06-30  
**Call / release date:** Release 2026-08-05; supplemental on IR

## Sources

- **company release:** Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. Reports Results for the Second Quarter of 2026  
  https://www.hosthotels.com/Press-Releases/2026/PressRelease_28366 (`company release`)  
  Mirrored: `_raw/HST_Q2_2026_PressRelease.html`
- **8-K Item 2.02:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070750/000107075026000122/hst-20260805.htm (`8-K`) — exhibits 99.1 release / 99.2 supplemental

---

## Capital headline

Host delivered a **rate-led owner-operator beat**: comparable hotel RevPAR **+7.0%** to **$251.53** and Total RevPAR **+5.9%**, with leisure transient + group strength and a FIFA World Cup overlay. Management **raised FY 2026 comparable RevPAR and Total RevPAR growth to 4.75%–5.25%**. Capital story is recycling + ROI CapEx (Marriott/Hyatt transformational programs; Grand Hyatt Washington completed in Q2) plus a fortress IG balance sheet ($5.1B debt, **no 2026 maturities**, ~$3.6B liquidity) after a large special dividend funded by Four Seasons–related taxable gains. Wage pressure is acknowledged but **offset by rate** in the quarter — watch 2H margin guide for labor stickiness.

## Operating KPIs (company-reported only)

| Comparable hotel RevPAR | **$251.53** | $235.05 | **+7.0%** | company release |

| Comparable hotel EBITDA | **$497M** | — | +7.8% | company release |
| Comparable hotel EBITDA margin | **31.9%** | — | +60 bps | company release |
| GAAP net income | **$241M** | $225M | +7.1% | company release |
| GAAP operating profit margin | **17.9%** | — | +40 bps | company release |
| Diluted EPS | **$0.35** | $0.32 | +9.4% | company release |
| EBITDAre | **$519M** | $491M | +5.7% | company release |
| Adjusted EBITDAre | **$525M** | $496M | **+5.8%** | company release |

**YTD 2026:** comparable RevPAR $247.84 (+5.7%); Total RevPAR $417.89 (+5.3%); Adj. EBITDAre $1,068M (+5.7%); GAAP NI $742M (`company release`).

**Business mix (Q2 room nights vs 2025):** Transient room nights −0.7% but transient room revenue **+6.9%**; Group room nights **+3.5%**, group revenue **+7.4%**; Contract room nights +3.4%, revenue +6.6% (`company release`). FY2025 mix context: transient / group / contract ~61% / 34% / 5% of room sales (`company release`).

CBD +16.5%; Northern Virginia +15.8%; Maui +13.6%; Miami +13.1%; Chicago +11.9%; San Francisco/San Jose +9.8%; New Orleans **−6.9%**; Denver −2.6%; Seattle −2.6%; Orlando −3.1% (`company release` location tables). All-locations comparable OCC **74.9%** (vs 74.1%); ADR **$335.83** (vs $317.39) (`company release`).

## Outlook & guidance

**Raised FY 2026** (`company release`):

| NAREIT FFO / share | $2.11–$2.14 | $2.06–$2.12 | +$0.02 mid |
| Adjusted FFO / share | $2.15–$2.18 | $2.10–$2.16 | +$0.03 mid |

Management notes: July comparable RevPAR **~+10%** vs 2025 with World Cup boost; 2H assumes leisure durability + modest short-term group improvement; dispositions reduce earnings vs 2025; condo sales at Four Seasons Orlando adjacent development contribute estimated **$16–$20M** to NI / Adj. EBITDAre in 2026; no incremental hurricane BI beyond 1Q already received (`company release`).

## Supply, pipeline, renovations / CapEx

- Portfolio: **70 U.S. + 5 international** properties ≈ **41,300 rooms**; plus interests in seven domestic JVs (`company release` About)  
- **CapEx YTD / FY forecast** (`company release`):

| Category | YTD 2026 | FY 2026 forecast range |

| Renewals & replacements (R&R) | **$138M** | **$275–$315M** |

| **Total capital allocation** | **$259M** | **$567–$647M** |

Note: Release CapEx table also breaks out Marriott/Hyatt Transformational vs other ROI; YTD Transformational spend cited as **$73M** with FY Transformational high-end **$175M** (`company release`). Sub-line arithmetic in the HTML table was ambiguous — prefer the **Total ROI / Total capital allocation** rows above.

- Grand Hyatt Washington transformational renovation **completed Q2 2026** (5 of 6 Hyatt Transformational Capital Program hotels done) (`slides` / `company release`)  
- Expect **$19M** operating guarantees in 2026 under Marriott/Hyatt transformational programs; Q2 guarantees received to offset disruption (`company release`)  
- Hawaii Kona Low rainstorm: estimated property costs **~$27–$32M** incl. remediation; insurance expected to cover substantially above deductible; hotels remained operational (`company release`)  
- Dispositions: sale of six hotels in 2025–2026 weighs on Adj. EBITDAre comps; Sheraton Parsippany sold in Q2 (footnote in reconciliations) (`company release`)  
- Four Seasons Orlando adjacent condo: seven villas sold contributed **$8M** to Q2 NI and Adj. EBITDAre (`company release`)

**supply note:** transformational CapEx ROI vs disruption; Hawaii remediation; disposition recycling pace.

## Balance sheet / debt / refinancing

As of **2026-06-30** (`company release`):

- Total assets **$13.3B**  
- Debt **$5.1B**; WA maturity **4.7 years**; WA interest **4.8%**; **no maturities in 2026**  
- Liquidity **~$3.6B** incl. FF&E escrow **$156M** and **$1.5B** undrawn revolver capacity  
- Cash & equivalents **$1,953M** (balance sheet); Jul 15 payment of regular + special dividend reduced cash by **$630M**  
- Dividend: Q2 **$0.92**/share paid Jul 15, 2026 (includes **$0.72** special ≈ **$500M** taxable gain distribution from Four Seasons sales completed 1Q 2026)  
- Shares: ~685.0M outstanding at quarter-end (`company release` balance sheet)

**capital note:** IG credit unchanged narrative; special dividend vs dry powder for acquisitions; no 2026 wall.

## Labor / talent / cost

- Higher room rates **offset wage expense increases** in Q2; GAAP margin +40 bps despite wages and lower insurance gains (−$9M net insurance gains y/y) (`company release`)  
- Comparable hotel EBITDA margin +60 bps despite higher incentive management fees and lower attrition/cancellation fees / operating profit guarantees vs 2025 (`company release`)  
- FY guide: 1H rate gains offset wage expense; 2H y/y rate growth expected to **moderate** (`company release`)  
- No discrete wage % or staffing FTE metrics disclosed in the release tables

**talent note:** qualitative wage inflation confirmed; quantify via 10-Q expense lines if needed.

## Segment / brand / geography mix

- Premium branded portfolio (Marriott, Hyatt, Hilton, Fairmont, etc.) — Host owns real estate; brands operate (`company release` About)  
- Growth broad-based: markets **with and without** World Cup matches both solid (`company release`)  
- Soft spots: New Orleans, Denver, Seattle, Orlando (comparable RevPAR down) — group/city calendar and local idiosyncratic (`company release` tables)  
- International (5 hotels): RevPAR +6.4%, Total RevPAR +6.7% (`company release`)

## Capital Graph signal proposals (decision support)

1. **Signal:** U.S. luxury/upper-upscale owner RevPAR +7% with guide raised to ~5% FY — rate over occupancy.  
   **Domain:** D1  
   **Evidence:** company release comparable RevPAR +7.0%; FY guide 4.75–5.25%  
   **Implication:** Deploy/redeploy into rate-elastic resort + CBD assets still clearing; underwrite ADR durability post-World Cup.  
   **Lane:** demand

2. **Signal:** Group room revenue +7.4% / room nights +3.5% — group recovery alive at Host quality tier.  
   **Domain:** A* / D1  
   **Evidence:** company release business mix table  
   **Implication:** Convention CBD residual value supported near-term; still market-selective (contrast New Orleans −6.9%).  
   **Lane:** demand | supply

3. **Signal:** $525–$600M R&R+ROI CapEx with Marriott/Hyatt transformational guarantees ($19M 2026).  
   **Domain:** C2 (supply/renovation)  
   **Evidence:** company release CapEx table + guarantees commentary  
   **Implication:** CapEx is the growth CapEx — ROI underwriting must net disruption + guarantee offsets.  
   **Lane:** supply | capital

4. **Signal:** IG BS — $5.1B debt, no 2026 maturities, ~$3.6B liquidity after funding ~$500M special dividend.  
   **Domain:** E2  
   **Evidence:** company release Balance Sheet / Dividends  
   **Implication:** Dry powder for selective M&A remains; special dividend shows willingness to return disposition gains.  
   **Lane:** capital

5. **Signal:** Wage inflation visible but margin expansion (+60 bps hotel EBITDA margin) via rate.  
   **Domain:** D1 / talent labor  
   **Evidence:** company release Highlights  
   **Implication:** If 2H rate decelerates as guided, margin defense becomes the swing factor for FFO.  
   **Lane:** talent | demand

6. **Signal:** World Cup / July ~+10% RevPAR — event residual into Q3 guide.  
   **Domain:** A*  
   **Evidence:** company release Outlook  
   **Implication:** Separate event uplift from run-rate when comparing Host to non-host-city REITs.  
   **Lane:** demand

## What Hal should decide / watch

- Post–World Cup RevPAR fade vs guide midpoint.  
- Whether disposition proceeds are redeployed into acquisitions or further buybacks/dividends (guidance assumes no further deals).  
- Transformational CapEx IRRs vs construction cost inflation.  
- Maui recovery path (still called out as uncertain timing).  
- Labor: can rate still outrun wages in 2H?

## Quotes worth keeping

> “We achieved comparable hotel RevPAR growth of 7.0% for the quarter, driven by solid rate growth across the portfolio, bolstered by the World Cup and broad-based strength in leisure transient demand and group business.” — James F. Risoleo, President & CEO (`company release`)

> “As a result, we are increasing our 2026 comparable hotel Total RevPAR and RevPAR growth guidance ranges to 4.75% to 5.25% over 2025.” — Risoleo (`company release`)

# Pebblebrook Hotel Trust (PEB) — Q2 2026 Earnings Digest

**Classification:** editor-authored digest of public IR — decision support

**Period:** Quarter ended 2026-06-30  
**Call / release date:** Release 2026-07-29; conference call 2026-07-30 09:00 ET

## Why this REIT (third digest)

Clearest public Same-Property RevPAR / ADR / OCC package among {PEB, RHP, APLE, PK} with a fully fetchable IR release (hotel EBITDA, leverage, maturity wall, disposition math, and raised FY outlook) — best cite density for a v0 Capital Graph digest without a paywalled transcript.

## Sources

- **company release (IR):** Pebblebrook Hotel Trust Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results  
  https://investor.pebblebrookhotels.com/news-1/news-releases/news-details/2026/Pebblebrook-Hotel-Trust-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx (`company release`)  
  Mirrored: `_raw/PEB_Q2_2026_release.html`

- **Org dossier:** orgs/pebblebrook.md (capital lens only — no STR invented)
- **Transcript:** not opened (call replay may be on IR webcast archive)

---

## Capital headline

Pebblebrook printed a **beat-and-raise owner quarter** driven by Same-Property RevPAR **+6.5%** (ADR +4.7%, OCC +1.7 pts) and Hotel EBITDA **+7.1%** with **67 bps** margin expansion — expense growth (+3.8%) lagged revenue (+4.8%). Resorts (+12.0% RevPAR) and San Francisco (+16.0%) carried growth; **Washington, DC (−9.9%)** and urban San Diego (−9.1%) were the known weak spots. Balance-sheet de-lever continues (net debt / TTM corporate EBITDA **5.3x**), Dec-2026 converts **fully reserved**, and capital return mixes buybacks with preferred retirement at a discount via the Chamberlain West Hollywood sale. For Capital Graph: this is a **lifestyle urban + resort** beta with SF recovery and DC government softness as the paired A* / supply signals — not a Host-like group CBD bellwether.
